id_and_class.theory_title: Ismael's Reflexive Representation and Situated Self
id_and_class.summary: Jenann Ismael explains the first-person structure of consciousness through reflexive representation: a mental state can represent the world while also presenting its own occurrent character, which gives experience its immediacy, privacy, and ownership. She treats phenomenal concepts as indexical, like ‘I’ and ‘now’, so the explanatory gap is a predictable feature of self-locating representation rather than evidence for dualism. She does not claim that self-representation produces phenomenal experience, and leaves the question of why it feels like anything open.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Subjectivity as the Reflexive Surface of Thought

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Ismael identifies the first-person structure of experience with a dual-content architecture in which states represent the world and present themselves; she calls the phenomenal field the ‘reflexive surface’ of thought, but does not identify phenomenality itself with this architecture.
conceptual_ground.ontological_status: Physicalism (non-reductive in an epistemic and semantic sense)
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Minds are high-level information-processing systems implemented in biological dynamics, like virtual machines, without point-for-point mapping onto neural parts. The gap between physical and phenomenal description is epistemic, with no ontological gap behind it.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Self-consciousness and the first-person perspective arise from reflexive architecture in an embodied system, but Ismael leaves the source of phenomenal quality unresolved.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Ordinary intentional content points beyond the state, while presentational content comes from properties of the state itself. Subjectivity arises when a state is used as a demonstrative exemplar of itself (‘this experience’), which explains immediacy, authority, and the sense that experiences belong to their subject.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Phenomenal concepts are grounded in displayed exemplars: one learns what an experience is like by having it. Qualia resist objective description because science abstracts away from perspective while phenomenal concepts depend on one, but Ismael does not claim this explains why there is any feel at all.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Physical systems, embodied agents with internal models of world and self, representational states with intentional and presentational content, and high-level virtual-machine organization.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: First-person access works by self-location, like finding ‘you are here’ on a complete map. Third-person science can describe a state fully without supplying the reflexive identification that comes from occupying it.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: An embodied agent’s evolving model of its location, body, history, goals, and expectations, coupled to its world-model in a recursively updating loop; the self is a dynamically maintained perspective within that system.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Self-consciousness, first-person knowledge, the explanatory gap, and the structure of subjectivity; phenomenality is left unreduced.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Dual content: one state carries both intentional content about the world and presentational content about itself, so the system can identify its own occurrent states from within.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Self-representation and world-representation update each other continuously, since the agent’s actions change its next sensory input.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In the high-level organization of an embodied information-processing system rather than in particular neural components.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Conscious experience belongs to a high-level control interface through which the agent integrates information, remembers, anticipates, and regulates action.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Perceptual inputs are integrated into one evolving internal model of the agent’s situation, from which the agent occupies an implicitly represented position.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Representation is central, and the key move is reflexive: the representing state enters its own representational scope instead of being described by a separate higher-order state.
core_claims_and_evidence: Knowing what an experience is like resembles locating oneself on a map, since complete objective information does not by itself tell you which state is yours or ‘here’.
Mary learns a new way of identifying a state already described physically, so the knowledge argument does not establish a nonphysical property.
Self-consciousness is a formal capacity of a medium to take its own contents as objects, while consciousness is a qualitative property only some such media have.
Perspectives in relational quantum mechanics need not belong to conscious observers, so quantum theory supports her account of embedded perspective without generating consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical, drawing on philosophy of language (indexicals), cognitive architecture, and philosophy of physics.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Critics question whether the presentational domain can be specified without circularity, since the account must say which aspects of a state figure in self-representation and why. Ismael herself criticizes self-representational theories, such as Kriegel’s, when they claim to define consciousness.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: If reflexive architecture can occur without phenomenality, the theory does not say what separates a conscious self-representing system from an equally sophisticated nonconscious one. It diagnoses the hard problem’s epistemic structure more than it solves its metaphysical core.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent with naturalism and avoids both dualism and reductive representationalism, at the cost of leaving the ontological source of experience open.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Ismael holds that artificial systems could in principle have self-consciousness without consciousness, and her theory does not say what would add the qualitative side.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since the self is a perspective maintained within an embodied physical system rather than a Cartesian substance, nothing in the view supports its persistence after that system stops.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The account is naturalistic and places agents within physics without any cosmic purpose.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Virtual-machine organization could in principle run on another substrate, but whether the copy would be phenomenally conscious is exactly the question Ismael leaves open.
